title: FTSE Russell US indexes — the first December semi-annual reconstitution: full cap-tier migration, reduced style/float scope, effective at the open 2026-12-14
source: EST: owner-published date, stated FOUR independent times and filed estimate only because this calendar's confirmed-tier prefixes have no member for an index owner's own schedule (see notes). (1) FTSE Russell's reconstitution page, lseg.com/en/ftse-russell/russell-reconstitution, re-fetched direct by this session 2026-09-06 (HTTP 200, 228,333 bytes, 13,561 characters of text extracted in-session): "The newly reconstituted indexes take effect after US market close on December 11", and in its FAQ "The newly reconstituted indexes take effect after the market close on December 11, 2026." (2) FTSE Russell, "Russell US Equity Indexes" construction and methodology, v7.2, August 2026 (lseg.com dam PDF, HTTP 200, 746,491 bytes, 52 content streams inflated and text-extracted in-session), section 4.2.3: "Reconstitution occurs on the fourth Friday in June and the second Friday in December"; section 9.3.1 repeats "second Friday in December"; Appendix F's schedule table gives Implementation = "2nd Friday of December", Rank Day = "Last business day of October", Preliminary Information Released = "Four weeks prior to implementation". (3) FTSE Russell, "FAQ Document Russell US Equity 2026", July 2026 (lseg.com dam policy-documents PDF, HTTP 200, 198,134 bytes, text-extracted in-session), which publishes a COMPLETE dated December 2026 calendar column -- market-cap data cut-off 30 October 2026, indicative review products circulated 13 November 2026, query period 16-27 November 2026, lock-down open 30 November 2026, style capping cut-off 2 December 2026, Review Effective Date (open of) 14 December 2026 -- and states "Implementation: Semi-annual reconstitution changes are implemented after the close on the last Friday in June and the second Friday in December." (4) REPRODUCED FROM THE RULE: December 2026's Fridays are 12-04 / 12-11 / 12-18 / 12-25, so the second is 2026-12-11; October 2026's last business day is Friday 10-30; and 2026-11-13 to 2026-12-11 is exactly 28 days, matching the four-week rule to the day, with the FAQ's 4 = 2 (query) + 2 (lockdown) split internally consistent. Appendix F defines implementation as "the day changes are made after the close of the market and become effective at the open on the Monday following" -- Monday 2026-12-14, which the FAQ states independently as the Review Effective Date. Promote to confirmed when this calendar gains a prefix for an index owner's own published schedule. notes: THE SCOPE IS NOT THE SAME AS JUNE'S, and that is the single most decision-relevant fact about this entry -- it is rule-sourced, not inferred. Ground rules v7.2 Appendix F carries a second table, "Reconstitution updates", comparing the June and December legs line by line. Three legs are FULL in December: total market cap (movement between market-cap indexes), nationality/country assignment, and total shares outstanding used for ranking. Three are REDUCED. Float adjustments: June applies none (section 9.3.2, "no buffers will be observed ... float updates will be implemented regardless of size") while December is "Applied with a 3% buffer" (section 9.3.3, "For the December review, no buffers will be observed for ranking total capitalization. However, free float updates will be implemented with observation of the 3% buffers"). Style probability: June re-scores the whole universe; December covers only "New Adds to R3000E, including IPOs added between rank dates" plus movements between R1000/R2000 and R2000/Microcap -- the owner's page says the same verbatim, "During the December reconstitution, style probabilities are updated for new additions or membership movements ... not on the entire universe of securities." Voting rights: December makes "No adjustments or further research on existing members". So the cap-tier migration leg lands in full and the style-index and float-reweighting legs largely do not. SIZING, FROM THE OWNER'S OWN NUMBER: FTSE Russell's "Impacts of the Russell US Reconstitution" PDF (lseg.com dam, HTTP 200, 444,549 bytes, text-extracted in-session) puts Russell 2000 reconstitution turnover at an average of 12.8% of base market value across 252 stocks for 2004-2026, down from 32.0% / 534 stocks for 1996-2003. That annual figure is what now splits across two dates. December 2026's drift window is SIX months (rank day 2026-04-30 to rank day 2026-10-30), not twelve. THE CORRIDOR: 2026-12-11 is already the date of two `high` entries -- cr-expiry-2026-12-11 and government-funding-deadline-2026-12-11 -- one day after cpi-2026-12-10 (high) and two after fomc-2026-12-09 (high), with opex-2026-12-18 (high) the following Friday. That collision is why impact is medium rather than low, and it is also why whole-day ETF volume cannot score this date: 22 tracked events sit within five days of it. Impact medium, status estimate: it widens caution about the 2026-12-11 close and the 2026-12-14 open and licenses nothing. `symbols` is deliberately EMPTY, not an oversight -- the flow is in the underlying names migrating between the R1000 and R2000, and putting an ETF proxy here would make the deterministic screen trip on small-cap beta, which carries no information about reconstitution scope. Kind `sector` matches the sibling market-structure flow entries; the enum has no index-flow member and the imperfect fit is named, not fixed from this lane.
